name: bg-falling-stars

frames.best_why: Frame 4 has the densest spread of long white streaks reaching every edge, showing the warp clearly.

tagline: White streaks race outward from the centre like a jump to light speed.
summary: A dark full-bleed starfield drawn on a canvas: small dots in the middle stretch into long white lines as they fly toward the viewer and out past the edges, forever.
appearance: A pure black field filled with short white dashes that radiate from the centre. Near the middle they are tiny specks and near the edges they lengthen into bright streaks. A small white title and dim subtitle sit at the centre.
behaviour: Stars push steadily outward from the centre, growing longer as they near the viewer, then wrap back to the middle to start again. The loop never stops and only the resize event restarts the sizing.
demo_content: The heading 'Falling Stars' over the line 'Canvas-based 3D star field effect'.
search_phrases: canvas starfield for a space page
galaxy jump effect in the browser
use_when: A dark hero or space-themed page needs a constant sense of speed behind its headline.
avoid_when: It redraws on every frame forever and is absolutely positioned, so it needs a sized relative parent.
customise: color tints the stars and count sets how many there are; className adds styling, while speed, the three blur layers and projection are in the source.
weight_why: Two hundred stars drawn with several strokes each, on every animation frame.

a11y.note: Decorative canvas with no reduced-motion check and no way to pause the endless outward motion.

issues: The subtitle is faint grey on black and barely readable at this size.
polish_why: Convincing speed trails on a clean black field; otherwise a familiar starfield with a weak subtitle.
